column2: 古英语 sūþ ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sunþr ← 原始日耳曼语 *sunþrą ← 原始印欧语 *sóh₂wl̥（日）
column3: the direction opposite north
column5: They drove south for two hours.|The window faces south all day.
column6: the direction where the sun stands highest – 日头最高的那一侧
column7: 南：四个基本方位之一|南方：位于南边的那一片地区

column2: 古英语 sūþēast，由 south ＋ east 复合而成
column3: the direction midway between south and east
column5: The storm moved off to the southeast.|Their farm lies southeast of town.
column6: the point midway between two named directions – 两个方位之间的正中一点

column2: 古英语 sūþerne ← 原始日耳曼语 *sunþrōnijaz，由 south ＋ -ern 构成
column3: belonging to or coming from the south
column5: Southern winters are much milder.|She grew up in a southern port.
column6: belonging to the sunward side – 属于向日那一侧的
column7: 南方的：位于或来自南边的|南部的：属于某地南半部的

column2: 古英语 sūþwest，由 south ＋ west 复合而成
column3: the direction midway between south and west
column5: Rain came in from the southwest.|The road bends southwest after the bridge.
column6: the point midway between the other two – 另两个方位之间的正中一点

column2: 中古英语 sovereyn ← 古法语 soverain ← 俗拉丁语 *superānus ← 拉丁语 super（在上）；拼法受 reign 的俗解影响
column3: having supreme authority, or a ruler with such authority
column5: Parliament remains the sovereign body here.|The sovereign opened the session.
column6: standing above all others in authority – 权柄在众人之上
column7: 至高的：没有更高权力在其上|君主：掌握最高权力的统治者

column2: 「播种」一支 ← 古英语 sāwan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sēaną ← 原始印欧语 *seh₁-（播）；同形的「母猪」另出古英语 sugu
column3: to put seed into the ground so that it grows
column5: They sow wheat here every spring.|Doubt was sown among the members.
column6: putting seed into the ground – 把种子放进地里
column7: 播种：把种子种到地里|撒播：把种子或说法散开

column2: 古英语 spadu（铲）← 原始日耳曼语 *spadô
column3: a tool with a flat blade for digging
column5: He leaned on his spade and rested.|She played the ace of spades.
column6: a flat blade pushed into the ground – 压进地里的平刃
column7: 铲子：挖土用的平刃工具|黑桃：扑克牌四种花色之一

column2: 古英语 spann ← 原始日耳曼语 *spannō（一掌之宽）← 原始印欧语 *(s)pend-（张开）
column3: the full extent from one end to the other
column5: The bridge has a span of thirty metres.|His career spanned four decades.
column6: the reach stretched from end to end – 从一端张到另一端的那段距离
column7: 跨度：两端之间的距离|延续期：从头到尾的一段时间

column2: 古英语 spær（节省的、稀少的）← 原始日耳曼语 *sparaz ← 原始印欧语 *sph₁rós
column3: kept in reserve for later use, or to give from what one has
column5: Keep a spare key in the drawer.|Can you spare a few minutes.
column6: held back rather than used up – 留着没有用掉的
column7: 多余的：额外留存未派用途的|腾出：从自己所有中让出一部分

column2: 古英语 spearca ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sparkō，或出原始日耳曼语 *sparkaz（活跃的）← 原始印欧语 *sperg-（撒、洒）
column3: a tiny piece of burning material thrown out
column5: A spark set the dry grass alight.|Sparks flew from the grinding wheel.
column6: a tiny burning bit thrown off – 迸出来的一小点燃着的东西
column7: 火花：迸射的细小亮点|火星：燃着的极小颗粒

column2: 中古英语 sparkel，由 spark ＋ -le（指小与反复后缀）构成
column3: to give off quick bright flashes, as light on water does
column5: Dew sparkled on the morning grass.|Her eyes sparkled with amusement.
column6: giving off many tiny flashes – 不断发出许多细小的闪亮
column7: 闪耀：连续放出耀眼的光|闪光：短暂而反复的亮点

column2: 古英语 specan ← 更早的 sprecan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sprekan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sprekaną ← 原始印欧语 *spreg-（发声）
column3: to use the voice to express thoughts
column5: She spoke to him after the meeting.|He speaks three languages fluently.
column6: putting thought into voiced words – 把想法化成出声的话
column7: 说话：用言语表达|演讲：面向众人作正式发言

column2: 中古英语 speker，为古英语 spreca（说话者）换后缀而成，相当于 speak ＋ -er
column3: a device that produces sound, or a person giving a talk
column5: One speaker crackled during the concert.|The main speaker arrived late.
column6: what or who sends the voice out – 把声音送出去的那个人或物
column7: 扬声器：把电信号变成声音的器件|演讲者：向众人发言的人

column2: 古英语 spere ← 原始西日耳曼语 *speru ← 原始日耳曼语 *speru ← 原始印欧语 *sperH-
column3: a weapon with a long shaft and a pointed head
column5: He threw the spear at the target.|Fishermen once used spears here.
column6: a long shaft ending in a point – 一端收成尖的长杆
column7: 矛：带尖头的长柄兵器|长枪：同类的长杆刺击兵器

column2: 古英语 spǣċ／sprǣċ ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sprāku ← 原始印欧语 *spreg-（发声）
column3: a formal talk given to an audience, or the power of speaking
column5: His speech lasted twenty minutes.|The illness affected her speech.
column6: the act and faculty of putting words out – 说出话来这件事以及这项能力
column7: 演说：对众人所作的正式讲话|言语：说话这项能力或所说的话

column2: 古英语 spēd（顺遂、成功）← 原始西日耳曼语 *spōdi ← 原始日耳曼语 *spōaną（顺利）← 原始印欧语 *speh₁-（顺遂）
column3: the rate at which something moves
column5: The car picked up speed on the hill.|They worked at great speed.
column6: how fast ground is covered – 单位时间里走过多少路
column7: 速度：移动的快慢程度|快速：速度高这个性质

column2: 「拼写」一支 ← 中古英语 spellen ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 espeler ← 法兰克语 *spelōn，与本族古英语 spellian（讲述）合流；同形的「咒语」出古英语 spell（消息、故事）
column3: to name or write the letters of a word in order
column5: She spelled her surname for him.|How do you spell that word.
column6: naming the letters one after another – 把字母按次序一个个说出或写下
column7: 拼写：按字母顺序写出词|拼出：把词的字母逐个说出

column2: 15 世纪起见于记载，由 spell ＋ -ing 构成
column3: the way letters are arranged to form a word
column5: The spelling of that word varies.|Check the spelling before printing.
column6: the settled order of a word letters – 一个词字母排定的次序
column7: 拼法：某个词的字母写法|拼写法：一套拼写规则

column2: 16 世纪起见于记载，由 spice ＋ -y 构成
column3: strongly flavoured with hot spices
column5: The soup was too spicy for me.|They serve spicy noodles here.
column6: carrying the sharp bite of spice – 带着香料那股辣劲
column7: 辛辣的：味道刺激发辣|加了香料的：调入香料而味浓

column2: 中古英语 spiþre ← 古英语 spīþra ← 原始西日耳曼语 *spinþrijō，源自原始日耳曼语 *spinnaną（纺）
column3: a small eight-legged creature that spins webs
column5: A spider had spun a web overnight.|Most spiders are harmless to people.
column6: the eight-legged creature that spins – 会纺丝结网的八足小动物
column7: 蛛：会结网的八足小动物|蛛形动物：包含蜘蛛蝎子的一类节肢动物

column2: 古英语 spillan（毁、糟蹋）← 原始西日耳曼语 *spilþijan ← 原始日耳曼语 *spilþijaną ← 原始印欧语 *(s)pel-（裂开）
column3: to let liquid run out of a container by accident
column5: He spilled coffee on the report.|Oil spilled into the harbour.
column6: letting liquid escape over the edge – 让液体越过边沿跑出去
column7: 溢出：液体从容器里流出|洒出：不小心把液体泼出

column2: 古英语 spinnan ← 原始日耳曼语 *spinnaną ← 原始印欧语 *(s)penh₁-
column3: to turn round quickly, or to make thread from fibre
column5: The wheel spun for several seconds.|She spins wool into yarn.
column6: turning quickly about a centre – 绕中心快速打转
column7: 旋转：绕轴快速转动|纺线：把纤维捻成线

column2: 中古英语 spyne ← 古法语 espine ← 拉丁语 spīna（刺、脊骨）
column3: the line of bones down the back, or a sharp point on a plant
column5: She injured her spine in the fall.|The title runs down the spine.
column6: the row of bones running down the back – 沿背部排成一列的骨头
column7: 脊柱：背部由脊椎骨连成的支柱|书脊：书籍装订的那一侧

column2: 「吐」一支 ← 古英语 spittan（吐），拟声起源；同形的「烤肉铁签」另出古英语 spitu
column3: to force liquid out of the mouth
column5: He spat the bitter seed onto the ground.|A drop of spit hit the page.
column6: forcing something out through the lips – 从唇间用力送出去
column7: 吐出：把口中之物送出口外|唾液：口中分泌的液体

column2: 中古英语 spit，为 despit 的截头形 ← 古法语 despit ← 拉丁语 dēspectum（俯视、轻蔑），源自 dēspicere（鄙视）
column3: a wish to hurt or annoy someone deliberately
column5: She said it out of pure spite.|Old spite kept the two apart.
column6: the ill will felt from looking down on another – 出于轻蔑而生的害人之心
column7: 恶意：故意想害人的心思|怨恨：积存下来的不满与敌意

column2: 或为 plash 的变体，加了词首 s-
column3: to make liquid fly about in drops
column5: Rain splashed against the dark window.|Children splashed in the shallow pool.
column6: sending liquid flying in drops – 使液体成滴四散飞开
column7: 飞溅：液体四散射出|泼洒：把液体大片洒出

column2: 拉丁语 splendidus，由 splendēre（发光）＋ -idus 构成
column3: very impressive in appearance, or extremely good
column5: The hall looked splendid in candlelight.|That is a splendid idea.
column6: shining bright enough to impress – 亮到令人赞叹
column7: 壮丽的：宏伟华美令人赞叹|极好的：程度上非常好

column2: 借自荷兰语与低地德语 splitten（劈开），1567 年前后起见于英语
column3: to break or divide along a line
column5: He split the log with one blow.|The party split over the issue.
column6: breaking apart along a line – 沿一条线分成两边
column7: 劈开：用力沿纹路分开|分裂：整体分成对立的几部分

column2: 中古英语 spoilen ← 古法语 espoillier ← 拉丁语 spoliāre（掠夺、毁坏）
column3: to become unfit to use, or to ruin something
column5: Milk spoils quickly in this heat.|Rain spoiled the whole afternoon.
column6: being stripped of what made it good – 好处被剥去而不再可用
column7: 变质：食物等因久放而不能用|损坏：使某物失去应有的好处

column2: 由 spoke（speak 的过去分词）＋ -s- ＋ man 构成
column3: a man who speaks officially for a group
column5: A spokesman denied the whole report.|The spokesman read a short statement.
column6: the man who speaks on behalf of others – 代众人出面说话的人
